variants.name: System.Threading.Channels bounded channel
variants.implementation_notes: The canonical .NET realization is a bounded channel: Channel.CreateBounded<T>(new BoundedChannelOptions(n)) with the default BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait makes WriteAsync complete only when a slot is free - that await is the backpressure signal and it composes with cancellation. The classic queue-plus-Monitor structure is replaced by the channel's internal synchronization, and the consumer side is naturally demand-driven via ReadAllAsync()/await foreach. BoundedChannelFullMode.DropOldest/DropNewest/DropWrite convert the same bound into shedding; TryWrite/Post returning false is a lossy shed decision, not backpressure, so it must be deliberate.
pitfalls: CreateUnbounded<Frame>() hides the whole problem: the queue grows until the process dies, and nothing upstream is ever told to slow down.
Writing with TryWrite and ignoring the false return turns backpressure into silent data loss.
Omitting the CancellationToken on WriteAsync lets a full channel block a request path for as long as the consumer stalls.
A channel is process-local: it paces in-process producers only, so a broker or HTTP source still needs its own flow control.

variants.name: TPL Dataflow with BoundedCapacity
variants.implementation_notes: When the pipeline is composed of blocks rather than producer/consumer pairs, TPL Dataflow expresses the same bound as BoundedCapacity on DataflowBlockOptions: a full target declines or postpones offered messages instead of buffering, and the source block's propagation waits, which is the demand mechanism of the dataflow model. The classic hand-written queue disappears because the blocks own their input queues; the remaining decisions are the capacity per block, the MaxDegreeOfParallelism (in-flight work), and whether to use SendAsync (awaits, backpressures) or Post (returns false, sheds).
pitfalls: Post() ignores the return value and silently drops messages; SendAsync awaits the same capacity, so the two must not be mixed casually.
A block whose capacity is unbounded (the default) accumulates the backlog the bound was meant to prevent.
Greedy linking with several targets can starve a bounded target; the block keeps trying to offer and the pipeline stalls in surprising places.
TPL Dataflow is in-process only and, for .NET Framework/.NET Standard projects, a NuGet dependency - not the right tool for a single queue.
